_comment: Diplomacy (key F). standing runs -100 (hostile) to +100 (allied); start = day 1. tiers: the lowest standing for each tier. respects: the stat an envoy needs to impress them (7+ = +1 a day, 3 or less = -1). drift: standing change a day with no envoy, and floor = how low that drift alone can push it. Deals: gift (any standing, +standing for coin), intel (Neutral+), trade (Friendly+, a pact paying every day while standing stays above trade_breaks), aid (Friendly+, while a surge gathers against your land: it lands at half), cede (Allied: they hand over their province, which needs a governor). Every deal except trade needs an envoy posted. cooldown in days. perk: what Friendly standing does on its own. react: standing change when you claim land next to theirs, when land next to theirs is erased, or when you light a Wardlamp next to theirs. Expeditions can move standing too (data/expeditions.json "standing"). trouble: what a Hostile or Wary faction does to you every few days (the Concord; the Erasers from Chapter 2, which add the kinds burn (study or Insight lost) and spill (Ink lost); issue #28). color / ui_color: map and screen colours for factions added after Act 1.
_asks_comment: Faction asks (issue #131, scripts/faction_asks.gd): favours a faction asks of you. ask_rules: first = [min, max] days after the Command Table opens before a faction's first ask, gap = [min, max] days between one ask ending and the next offer, offer_days = how long an offer waits for an answer in Diplomacy (F) before it lapses, warn_days = the reminder before a deadline. Each faction's asks: id (unique, never reuse: saves keep it), name, tier (lowest standing tier it is offered at), below (optional: only offered while standing is under this tier), days (deadline once accepted), repeat (days before it can be offered again once it ends; 0 = once per campaign), text (the request, in their voice), done_text / fail_text (what they say after). kind and its fields: expedition (job: an expedition in data/expeditions.json with "ask" naming this ask; it is only on the Guildhall board while the ask is accepted, and a squad still out at the deadline gets to finish), raid (target: a faction; win a Raid mission on that faction's land), salvage (win a Salvage mission in a province next to this faction's home, or anywhere with near: false), fray (max: keep every province of yours next to this faction's home at or under this Fray until the deadline; needs at least one; offered only while all are at least 10 under), lamp (light a Wardlamp in a province of yours next to this faction's home; offered only while none of them has one), deliver (cost: hand it over from Diplomacy before the deadline), shun (rival: hold no trade pact with that faction until the deadline; accepting tears up a pact you already have and the rival takes it badly: rival_hit standing). reward: standing, resources (gilt, supplies, ink, insight, renown), mats (Forge materials, data/materials.json), boon (intel: +1 day surge warning for days; truce: no Concord trouble for days; ward: per_day Fray (negative) on your provinces next to their home for days), recruit (that person turns up at the south gate early). fail (missing the deadline): standing, fine (Gilt they take), trouble (true: the Concord makes trouble at the next dawn), hex (per_day Fray for days on your provinces next to their home; a Wardlamp cancels it). refuse: standing change for saying no, or for letting the offer lapse unanswered.

factions.name: The Mercenary Guild
factions.blurb: Sellswords who run the Gallows Ferry and charge both ways. They don't care who you are, only whether your coin is real and your people pull their weight.

perk.text: Guild scouts share the road: expeditions +10%

gift.name: Settle a tab
gift.text: You pay off a Guild tab nobody remembers running up. They remember now.

intel.name: Buy river gossip
intel.text: Bargemen hear everything. For a few days you hear it too: +1 day of surge warning.

trade.name: Share the ferry tolls
trade.text: A cut of every crossing at Gallows Ferry, paid at dawn.

aid.name: Hire sellswords for the line
aid.text: Guild blades hold the line. The coming surge lands at half strength.

cede.name: Ask for Gallows Ferry
cede.text: The Guild signs the ferry over, on the understanding that their barges cross free forever.

asks.name: Run a barge through the Saltreed cut
asks.text: The river's silting up and the Saltreed cut is the only way round. Something in the reeds has been eating barges. Put two of yours on deck, get it through, and the Guild remembers.
asks.done_text: Barge through, cargo dry, nobody eaten. The Guild pays like it means it.
asks.fail_text: The barge went through without you. Two deckhands didn't come out. The Guild has written your name in the other ledger.

asks.name: Lighten the Concord's strongboxes
asks.text: The Concord taxed our barges twice last month. Once for crossing, once for 'contemplating crossing'. Go take some of it back off their road. We'll know if you did. We always know.
asks.done_text: The Guild drinks to your health at the ferry. Loudly, where the Concord's clerks can hear.
asks.fail_text: No raid, no tithe, no story. The Guild expected better from people who keep a sword-bouncer on the payroll.

asks.name: Settle the ferry dues
asks.text: Your carts have crossed at Gallows Ferry all season on a promise. The Guild runs on promises the way a mill runs on sand. Pay the dues in full, in grain and coin.
asks.done_text: Paid. On time. In full. The bargemen start telling your people what they hear on the river.
asks.fail_text: The Guild collected the dues itself, with interest and a crowbar.

asks.name: Lend two blades for a Guild contract
asks.text: A Guild contract has gone sideways at the toll-forts and every free sword we have is on the river. Lend us two of yours for three days. You'll get them back with most of their fingers.
asks.done_text: Contract closed. And a smuggler who watched your people work at the forts has asked where she can find you.
asks.fail_text: The contract went to another crew. The Guild does not lend twice to people who won't lend once.

factions.name: The Gutterwood Coven
factions.wants: Left alone, and the Blank kept out of the woods.
factions.blurb: Witches who grow trees from discarded letters and decide who leaves the Gutterwoods. They dislike visitors, flags and anything that lets the Blank closer.

react.why_erased: The Blank ate land next to the woods
react.why_lamp: A Wardlamp lit near the woods

perk.text: Hedge-wards: your land next to the Gutterwoods frays 1 less a day

gift.name: Leave an offering
gift.text: A jar of ink and a coin at the treeline. Both are gone by morning.

intel.name: Read the leaves
intel.text: The witches read the paper-leaves for you. +1 day of surge warning for a few days.

trade.name: Stall at the witch-market
trade.text: Herbs, roots and strange ink from the witch-market, delivered at dawn.

aid.name: Ask for hedge-wards
aid.text: The Coven weaves wards along your border. The coming surge lands at half strength.

cede.name: Ask for the Gutterwoods
cede.text: The Coven lets your flag into the woods. They stay. They are watching the flag.

asks.name: Keep the white off the treeline
asks.text: Your land runs up against our trees. When it frays, the woods fray with it. Hold every acre of yours along the treeline at 45 Fray or less for six days and we will believe you mean to be neighbours.
asks.done_text: The witches walk your side of the treeline and leave knots of hair and ink on the fences. Your land there frays slower for a while.
asks.fail_text: The white got into the hedges. The Coven has hung a hex on your side of the treeline. A Wardlamp would burn it off.

asks.name: Light a lamp by the woods
asks.text: Dark land draws the Blank like spilled ink draws flies. Light a Wardlamp on your side of the treeline. We would light our own, but we prefer our fire to have opinions.
asks.done_text: The lamp burns. Something with four legs and a lot of opinions sat under it all night, and followed the lamplighters home.
asks.fail_text: No lamp. The Coven lit candles for the dark acres instead, which is what they do for the dead.

asks.name: Gather the fallen letters
asks.text: Where the Blank eats a place, the words fall out of it first. Letters, names, the odd recipe. Bring us what has fallen along the Saltreed edge before it is gone. We grow trees from them.
asks.done_text: The witches sort the letters by grief and plant the saddest ones first. They send roots and gall in thanks.
asks.fail_text: The letters rotted to blank paper before anyone came. The Coven buried them without you.

asks.name: No Guild barges in the woods
asks.text: The Guild has been cutting our oaks for barge-keels and paying in apologies. Sign nothing with them for eight days. If you already trade with them, stop.
asks.done_text: Eight days without a Guild keel in the woods. The Coven sends a cart of herbs and something that might be an apology for doubting you.
asks.fail_text: You signed with the Guild while you were promising us. The witches have long memories and nothing else to do with them.

asks.name: Pull the hedge-books out of the white
asks.text: Our sisters kept hedge-books in the farms along the treeline: what grows where, who is buried under which oak. The white is eating the farms. Go into its edge, next to our woods, and pull out what you can before the books forget themselves.
asks.done_text: Half the hedge-books came back legible. The witches read them aloud at the treeline all night, so the trees would remember too.
asks.fail_text: The farms went white with the books inside. The Coven held a wake for the pages. You were not invited.

factions.name: The Gilded Concord
factions.blurb: The bureaucratic empire that rules the capital and audits the Tithe Road. An unregistered town run by someone who crawled out of the Blank is, to them, a paperwork emergency.

react.why_claim: More unregistered land on their border

factions.drift_why: Unregistered and unrepentant: the Concord files against you daily

perk.text: Registered at last: no more audits, and the Tithe Road tolls go easy

gift.name: Pay an outstanding fine
gift.text: You pay a fine for something. The receipt says 'existing'.

intel.name: Bribe a clerk
intel.text: A clerk lets you read the survey reports. +1 day of surge warning for a few days.

trade.name: Toll exemption
trade.text: Your carts go up the Tithe Road untaxed. That alone pays.

asks.name: Pay the back-tithe
asks.text: NOTICE OF ARREARS. The settlement styling itself 'Hollowmark' owes the Concord one season of tithe, assessed in coin and grain. Payment within five days will be recorded as cooperation. Non-payment will be recorded.
asks.done_text: Receipt issued, stamped and countersigned. The auditors have been told to leave you alone. For now. In writing.
asks.fail_text: Non-payment has been recorded. A collection party is being assembled. They are very good at collecting.

asks.name: Sit for the census
asks.text: The Concord does not recognise Hollowmark. The Concord would, however, recognise Hollowmark's population, if two responsible persons presented themselves at the Tithe Road customs house to be counted. Bring your own ink.
asks.done_text: Counted, measured and filed. Hollowmark now exists on paper, which the Concord treats as the only place that matters.
asks.fail_text: Nobody presented themselves. The census lists Hollowmark as 'uninhabited, presumed hostile'. The tax-riders take that as an invitation.

asks.name: Sign nothing with the Guild
asks.text: The Mercenary Guild operates an unlicensed ferry and is under review. Associates of the Guild will be reviewed with it. Hold no agreement with them for ten days and the review may conclude that you were never associated.
asks.done_text: The review concludes that Hollowmark was 'not materially associated'. The clerk who wrote it seemed almost pleased.
asks.fail_text: You traded with the Guild under review. The Concord files you under 'associates'.

asks.name: Audit a Guild cargo
asks.text: The Concord requires an independent audit of Guild cargo at Gallows Ferry. 'Independent' meaning you. 'Audit' meaning you open the crates and bring us what is inside. A finder's fee is authorised.
asks.done_text: The audit is filed. Its findings are exactly what was in the crates. The finder's fee arrives with a receipt.
asks.fail_text: No audit. The Concord notes your 'reluctance to assist an inquiry' in a file that is getting thick.

asks.name: Keep the road towns standing
asks.text: Fraying land beside the Tithe Road depresses toll revenue and alarms the clerks. Hold every holding of yours along the road at 35 Fray or less for seven days. The Concord will regard it as civic responsibility.
asks.done_text: The road towns held. A Concord surveyor marks your land 'stable' and sends sappers to shore up the ditches.
asks.fail_text: The road frayed on your side. The Concord has re-graded your land from 'irregular' to 'liability'.

events.text: A Concord auditor arrives with a ledger and leaves with %d Gilt. The fine was for 'unlicensed survival'.
Concord tax-riders seize %d Supplies on the road from %s.
A Concord Erasure writ is read aloud in %s. Nobody believes it, but everyone remembers it. Fray +%d.

factions.name: The Abbey of Saint Ledger
factions.wants: The world written back, line by line. Lately, just a night's sleep.
factions.blurb: The monks of Saint Ledger's have copied the Great Ledger by hand for three hundred years, so the world could be written back if the capital's copy burned. Their Abbot has them copying day and night now, and the pages come out blank. They are proud, poor, frightened, and owe the Concord everything.

react.why_claim: Another flag on the Abbey's lands
react.why_erased: The Blank ate land beside the Abbey
react.why_lamp: A Wardlamp lit beside the Abbey

perk.text: The brothers copy your notes: research goes 15% faster

gift.name: Send candles and lamp oil
gift.text: A cart of Candleford wax and oil goes up the hill. The brothers can copy past Compline again.

intel.name: Ask the bell-watch
intel.text: From the bell tower the brothers see the white move a day before anyone else. +1 day of surge warning for a few days.

trade.name: Buy from the scriptorium
trade.text: The Abbey sells you ink and copied charters at dawn, and pays a tithe on what it sells through Hollowmark.

aid.name: Ring the bells for the line
aid.text: The Abbey rings its great bells against the coming surge. The Blank hates the sound: it lands at half strength.

cede.name: Ask for the Abbey grounds
cede.text: The Prioress signs the Abbey's lands into your keeping, on the understanding that the brothers keep their cells, their bells and their beer.

asks.name: Keep the copying hall in candles
asks.text: Brother Odo, writing for the Prioress. The hall burns two hundred candles a night and the Erasers have burned the barges again. Send wax and oil up the lake road within five days, and we will remember who kept the lamps lit.
asks.done_text: The candles arrive. Brother Odo sends a copied psalter in thanks, with a note that every page has words on it, he checked.
asks.fail_text: The hall went dark for three nights. The brothers copied by feel. Nobody at the Abbey has said your name since, which for monks is saying a great deal.

asks.name: Bring back the bell-metal
asks.text: The Erasers took the cracked tenor bell from the Bonefield chapel and mean to melt it for a pyre-pan. A bell is a bell, even cracked. Go onto their ground and take back what you can carry.
asks.done_text: Two hundredweight of bell-bronze comes back up the hill on a cart. The founders say it can be recast. The Prioress says nothing, but she sends the founders to you first.
asks.fail_text: The bell went into the pyre-pan. You could hear it crack from the Abbey, the brothers say.

asks.name: Copy the names under the hill
asks.text: Sister Osyth's tally is the only record of the people under the Bonefield. The Prioress wants it copied onto vellum before the Erasers burn the cloister to the ground. Send two who can read and keep a steady hand.
asks.done_text: Eleven thousand names, copied fair, in a house of God. And a young brother in an Eraser's coat came to watch them do it, and asked if he could come home with them.
asks.fail_text: Nobody came to copy the names. The Prioress has set the novices to it, and they are slow, and the Erasers are not.

asks.name: Light a lamp on the lake road
asks.text: The lake road between Candleford and the Abbey is dark from Vespers to Lauds and the white comes up it at night. A Wardlamp on your side of it would let the brothers walk to market without saying their prayers twice.
asks.done_text: The lamp burns all night. The brothers walk the lake road in pairs now, singing, which they say is for the Blank and which is mostly for them.
asks.fail_text: No lamp. Brother Odo walked the lake road after dark anyway and came back with white on his sleeve.

factions.name: The Erasers
factions.wants: The Ledger burned, the Concord forgotten, and the clean page Verity promised them.
factions.blurb: Verity Hale's followers: archivists, clerks and struck-out families who have read the Concord's unedited drafts and want every ledger burned. They wear white coats, carry tapers, and read aloud the names of the towns the Concord wrote out before they set the fire. They think you are pushing the white back for the wrong side.
factions.drift_why: You push the white back. To the Erasers, that is taking the Concord's side

react.why_claim: More land held against the clean page
react.why_erased: The white took land beside the Bonefield, as they prayed it would
react.why_lamp: A Wardlamp lit against the white

perk.text: The Readers leave you be: no Eraser trouble, and the drafts they share bring in 1 Insight a day

gift.name: Hand over a Concord ledger
gift.text: A Concord tax-ledger, unburned, left on the Bonefield wall. By morning it is ash and the Readers know who left it.

intel.name: Sit through a reading
intel.text: You listen to the Readers read the drafts aloud by the pyre. Most of it is names. Some of it is where Verity means to aim the white next: +1 day of surge warning for a few days.

asks.name: Give up the tithe-rolls
asks.text: First Reader Askew, to the person in charge at Hollowmark. Your tax office kept the Marches' tithe-rolls. Somebody has them. Hand them to the Bonefield to be read and burned, and the Readers will pass your towns by for a while.
asks.done_text: The tithe-rolls burn on the Bonefield wall. The Readers read every name aloud before the fire takes it. It takes all night.
asks.fail_text: The First Reader writes that she is disappointed, which for an archivist means she has opened a file on you.

asks.name: Send nothing up the hill
asks.text: The Abbey copies the lie that buried the Bonefield. Every candle you send up that hill keeps the lie going one more night. Hold no pact with them for eight days and the Readers will believe you have read the page.
asks.done_text: Eight days, and not a cart up the lake road. The Readers leave a burned page on the Hollowmark well: a name, and 'thank you' under it.
asks.fail_text: You traded with the Abbey while promising us. The First Reader adds your name to a list. She does not say which list.

events.text: Readers slip into Hollowmark by night and burn the Scriptorium's notes on %s. They leave the ash in a neat pile, labelled.
events.text_insight: Readers slip into Hollowmark by night and burn a crate of drafts: %d Insight's worth of notes. The ash is labelled.

events.text: Somebody has poured %d Ink into the well and painted the rim white. A taper is propped against it, still burning.
Readers stand in the square at %s and read the unedited drafts aloud all night. By morning half the town believes the white is a mercy. Fray +%d.

factions.name: The Velvet Nobility
factions.wants: The music to go on. The water to stay off the bridges. Nobody to ask what it costs.
factions.blurb: The old houses of the Velvet Causeway: dukes, marquises and their cousins, who own the bridges, the wine and each other's debts. When the Blank came they decided the masquerade should simply not stop. It has not stopped for a year, and every night a few guests go upstairs and do not come down.

react.why_claim: Another upstart flag on the lake shore
react.why_erased: The Blank ate land beside the Causeway
react.why_lamp: A Wardlamp lit beside the Causeway

perk.text: The Nobility take you up as their latest fashion: patronage brings in 4 Gilt a day

gift.name: Send a crate of the Terraces' best
gift.text: A crate of Vauclair red goes across the lake with your compliments. The Duc de Lantenay sends back a card that says the wine is 'interesting'. From him, that is a sonnet.

intel.name: Buy gossip at the masquerade
intel.text: Your envoy listens behind a fan all night. Most of it is who is sleeping with whom. Some of it is which bridge the ink came up last: +1 day of surge warning for a few days.

trade.name: Supply the masquerade
trade.text: Hollowmark sends candles, bread and ribbon across the lake every week, and the Nobility pay on time, which nobody expected.

aid.name: Borrow the bridge duellists
aid.text: The Causeway's duellists come to hold your line against the surge, in pairs, saluting. The Blank finds them very hard to get past: it lands at half strength.

cede.name: Ask for the Causeway's deeds
cede.text: The Duc de Lantenay signs the Causeway into your keeping with a flourish, on the understanding that the Nobility keep their houses, their titles and the best box at the opera.

asks.name: Keep the masquerade in wine
asks.text: The Duc de Lantenay presents his compliments to the person in charge at Hollowmark. The cellars of the Causeway are running low. Five days, a cart of wine and bread, and the Nobility will remember who kept the glasses full.
asks.done_text: The cart crosses the lake. That night, for the first time, somebody at the masquerade raises a glass to Hollowmark. Only one somebody, but a duke.
asks.fail_text: No cart. The Causeway drank water for a night. The Nobility will be talking about it for a generation.

asks.name: Snub the Concord
asks.text: The Concord sends its clerks to the masquerade to count the guests. The Nobility would like it understood that Hollowmark does not dine with clerks. Hold no pact with the Concord for eight days.
asks.done_text: Eight days, not a word to the Concord. The Nobility find this extremely chic. A bolt of velvet cord arrives, wrapped in a scandal sheet with your name in it.
asks.fail_text: You were seen dining with clerks. The scandal sheets are merciless.

asks.name: Keep the ink off the bridges
asks.text: Now that the masquerade is over, the Causeway must keep its feet dry the ordinary way. Keep the white back from every province of yours beside the Causeway for ten days, and the Nobility will be grateful in writing.
asks.done_text: Ten dry days. The Nobility send a letter of thanks written on actual paper, which on the Causeway is the highest honour there is.
asks.fail_text: The ink came up the steps of the opera house. The Nobility are sure it was your fault, and say so at length.

asks.name: Light the quay
asks.text: Lantern Quay is dark at night now that the Concord barges have stopped paying for the oil. A Wardlamp beside the Causeway would let the Nobility's boats come home without hitting anything, or anyone.
asks.done_text: The lamp burns all night across the water. The boatmen call it the Keeper's candle, and steer by it.
asks.fail_text: No lamp. A Nobility barge hit the quay in the dark, and a marquis went in the lake. He has not forgiven you.

events.text: A Causeway scandal sheet prints a story about Hollowmark's keeper and three duchesses. Settling the libel suit costs %d Gilt.
Velvet bravos 'borrow' %d Supplies from a cart out of %s, for a party. They leave a very charming note.
